title: Quarter to Seventy-Five
description: Episode 2 nocturnal drive as a song — no chorus, just the title phrase, a clock stuck at 3:44, and an FM needle drifting left.
stylePrompt: Slow ambient lullaby / detuned soft rock, ~65 BPM, drifting 4/4 with no clear downbeat (or soft 6/8 feel). Upright bass bowed underwater with long room reverb, vibraphone tremolo with occasional "missed" notes like a tired DJ, distant detuned soft-rock electric guitar through a dying amp (very quiet, never lead), music-box piano winding down, field recordings of windshield wipers and dashboard hum and FM needle drift as musical texture. Half-whispered solo vocal — intimate, sleepy, Rubella-adjacent — optionally dual-tracked as "driver" (close, dry) and "radio" (thin AM bandwidth, more plate reverb, slightly late). No big chorus; the hook is the title phrase repeating like a station ID. Bridge: 8 bars of only static and a single streetlamp buzz. Ends without resolution — fade on the groove as if the car keeps going. Mood: Empty Highway Confession, Ep2 nocturnal drive. Reference: Morphine underwater bass, late-night public radio jazz drift, Les Ondes Courtes sibling energy but English and softer. Use my Rubella voice; optional second pass as thin radio double.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Yellow lines like lullabies
Bass and treble lose the fight
Half-conscious heart on drift
Dashboard glow the only light
Windshield keeps a sleepy time
Streetlamps stretch and blur and climb

[Hook]
Quarter to seventy-five and low
The DJ's gone but the static knows
Carry my heart on the signal fade
Don't pull over, don't pull over

[Verse 2]
Same café three times or four
Clock stuck open at three forty-four
FM needle drifts to the left
Bass walking soft like underwater theft
I pass the exit, miss it twice
The groove is gentle and the canyon's nice

[Hook]
Quarter to seventy-five and low
The DJ's gone but the static knows
Carry my heart on the signal fade
Don't pull over, don't pull over

[Verse 3 — Dual: Driver + Radio]
(Driver) I should find a place to sleep
(Radio) The road is rocking you like a cradle
(Driver) Yellow lines still counting sheep
(Radio) Every reflector monotonous and faithful
(Together) Half-conscious heart on drift
(Together) Quarter to seventy-five and low

[Bridge — Static Only]
(Streetlamp buzz)
(Windshield wipe)
(FM hiss)
(Barely whispered) Don't pull over...

[Verse 4 — Sparse]
Now the piano is a music box
Winding down, losing the locks
City is a cough way up north
I become the music, become the road

[Final Hook — Fading]
Quarter to seventy-five and low
Quarter to seventy-five and low
The static knows
Don't pull over
Don't pull over
(fade — car keeps going)
notes:
## Production notes
- **Episode placement:** Episode 2, Empty Highway Confession / nocturnal drive (approx. 00:10:41–end of poetic half). Scores Radio Voice needs; sibling to *Les Ondes Courtes* (English, slower, no accordion costume). Also usable under “Static Between Stations” EyeWash overnight block.
- **Emotional arc:** Fog → hypnotic drift → dual driver/radio almost-clarity → pure static bridge → unresolved fade. No catharsis; the car does not stop.
- **Reference artists:** Morphine — *The Night*; Ep2 transcript poetry (primary lyric DNA); late-night public-radio jazz drift; weeks_of_fire — *Les Ondes Courtes*.
- **Runtime target:** ~2:30–3:00; can loop the hook + verse for longer drive montages.
- **Mix note for Minimax:** Emphasize bowed bass and vibraphone; keep guitar under the vocal; static must stay musical, not noisy.
